dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Reciprocity Act, 1943
Key Features
•	Principle of Reciprocity: Incorporates the principle of reciprocal treatment in specified legal matters between India and foreign countries. 
•	Government Notification: Empowers the Central Government to apply the provisions of the Act through notifications in respect of foreign States. 
•	Reciprocal Rights and Restrictions: Enables the extension of legal rights, privileges, exemptions, or the imposition of corresponding restrictions based on the treatment accorded to Indian citizens or entities abroad. 
•	Application to Foreign States: Applies to countries or territories notified by the Central Government under the Act. 
•	Promotion of Equality in International Relations: Facilitates fair and reciprocal legal treatment between India and other jurisdictions.

For the purpose of ascertaining the position of the working, actual or prospective, of any mine or abandoned mine, or for any other purpose connected with this Act or the rules made thereunder, any officer authorised, by the Central Government in this behalf, by general or special order, may--
(a) enter and inspect, at all reasonable times, any mine;
(b) weigh, draw samples or take measurements of the stocks of minerals recovered from any mine;
(c) survey and take samples and measurements in any such mine;
(d) examine any document, book, register or record in the possession or power of any person having the control of, or connected with, any mine and place marks of identification thereon and take extracts from, or make copies of, such document, book, register or record;
(e) order the production of any such document, book, register and record, by the person referred to in clause (d); and
(f) examine any person having the control of, or connected with, any mine.
(2) Any authorised officer may, for the purpose of ascertaining whether or not the requirements of this Act or any rule made thereunder have been complied with, either with, or where it is not possible to obtain warrant conveniently, then, without, a warrant,--
(a) search any mine;
(b) stop or board and search any vessel which is engaged or which is likely to be engaged in any activity regulated under this Act; and
(c) require the person for the time being having command or charge of mine or such vessel to produce any licence, permit, log book or other document relating, to the vessel or mine and examine or take copies of such licence, permit, log book or other document, as the case may be, for ascertaining the requirements of sub-section (1).
(3) Where the authorised officer has reason to believe that any vessel or mine has been, or is being, or is about to be, used or employed, as the case may be, in violation of any provision of this Act or rule made thereunder, he may, with, or where it is not possible to obtain warrant conveniently, then, without, a warrant,--
(a) seize and detain such vessel or mine, including any gear, equipment, stores or cargo found on board such vessel or belonging to the vessel and seize any mineral found on board the vessel;
(b) seize any evidence relating to violation of any provision of this Act or rule made thereunder;
(c) require the person for the time being having command or charge of the vessel, platform or erection of the mine so seized or detained to bring such vessel, platform or erection to any specified port;
(d) arrest any person whom such officer has reason to believe, has committed such violation:
Provided that the authorised officer, after arresting such person and before producing him before the competent court, shall inform the administering authority regarding the arrest and grounds of arrest communicated to the person so arrested.
(4) In taking any action under sub-section (3), the authorised officer may use such force as may be reasonably necessary.
(5) Where any vessel or other things are seized or detained, under sub-section (3),--
(a) the vessel or other things so seized or detained shall, as soon as possible, be produced before the court competent to try an offence under this Act and the court shall make such order as it may deem fit for the retention or custody of such vessel or things with the Central Government or any other authority pending the completion of any proceedings for the prosecution of any offence relating to such vessel or things, as the case may be, under this Act or rules made thereunder:

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Betwa River Board Act, 1976
Objective
The Betwa River Board Act, 1976 was enacted to establish the Betwa River Board for the construction of the Rajghat Dam and creation and regulation of the Rajghat Reservoir (now Rani Laxmibai Sagar) on the inter-State Betwa River. The Act aims to ensure coordinated development, management, and utilisation of the river's water resources by the Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh under the supervision of the Central Government. 
Key Provisions
•	Establishment of the Betwa River Board: Constitutes the Betwa River Board as a body corporate to implement and supervise the Rajghat Dam Project. 
•	Executive Committee: Provides for the constitution of an Executive Committee to assist the Board in carrying out its functions efficiently. 
•	Functions and Powers: Empowers the Board to plan, construct, operate, maintain, and regulate the Rajghat Dam, reservoir, irrigation works, and associated power generation facilities. 
•	Finance and Administration: Establishes the Betwa River Board Fund and provides for the preparation of budgets, maintenance of accounts, audit, and annual reports. 
•	Central Government Control: Empowers the Central Government to issue policy directions to the Board and resolve disputes between the Board and the participating State Governments. 
•	Entry and Protection: Authorises the Board to enter land for the discharge of its functions and protects actions taken in good faith under the Act. 
•	Rule-making Power: Empowers the Central Government to make rules and the Board to frame regulations for implementing the provisions of the Act.

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Prasar Bharati (Broadcasting Corporation of India) Act, 1990:
Objective
•	Establish the Prasar Bharati (Broadcasting Corporation of India)
•	Define its composition, functions, and powers
Key Provisions
1.	Establishment
•	Prasar Bharati (Broadcasting Corporation of India) established by the Central Government
•	Body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal
•	Headquarters in New Delhi with potential offices elsewhere in India and abroad (with Central Government approval)
2.	Composition of the Board
•	Chairman
•	Executive Member
•	Member (Finance)
•	Member (Personnel)
•	6 Part-time Members
•	Ex Officio Members:
•	Director-General (Akashvani)
•	Director-General (Doordarshan)
•	Representatives:
•	1 from the Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting
•	2 from the employees of the Corporation (elected)
3.	Appointments
•	Chairman and other Members (except ex officio, nominated, and elected members) appointed by the President of India on the recommendation of a committee.
•	Committee for Recommendations consists of:
•	Chairman of the Council of States (Chairman of the Committee)
•	Chairman of the Press Council of India
•	Nominee of the President of India
4.	Term of Office
•	Chairman: Part-time, 3 years or until 70 years of age, whichever is earlier.
•	Whole-time Members (Executive, Finance, Personnel): 6 years or until 62 years of age (for Finance and Personnel), 5 years or until 65 years of age (for Executive, as amended).
•	Part-time Members: 6 years, with one-third retiring every 2 years.
•	Elected Members: 2 years or until they cease to be employees.
5.	Powers and Functions
•	Executive Member: Chief Executive, exercises powers delegated by the Board.
•	Board: General superintendence, direction, and management of the Corporation.
6.	Removal and Suspension
•	Chairman and Members (except ex officio, nominated, and elected) can only be removed by the President of India on the ground of misbehavior after a Supreme Court inquiry.
•	Suspension possible pending inquiry.
7.	Other
•	Committees and Associations: Corporation can form committees and associate persons for advice.
•	Immunity of Proceedings: No act of the Board or committee invalidated by vacancies, defects in constitution, or appointment irregularities (unless affecting the merits of the case).

(a) "law providing for the prevention of hoarding or profiteering" means any law, or any order, rule or notification having the force of law, providing for--

(ii) the control of price at which any essential commodity may be brought or sold;
